title: SAT Math 2 — Linear Functions and Graphs Quiz
question: Five SAT-style questions on linear functions and graphs, with full working.
intro: Five questions on linear functions and graphs. **Show your working before you choose or type an answer.**

questions.title: Two values of a linear function
questions.prompt:
For the linear function \(f\):

\[f(2) = 7\]

\[f(6) = 19\]

What is \(f(10)\)?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} m &= \frac{19 - 7}{6 - 2} \\ &= 3 \end{aligned}\]

From \(x = 6\) to \(x = 10\) is 4 more units:

\[\begin{aligned} f(10) &= 19 + 4 \cdot 3 \\ &= \boxed{31} \end{aligned}\]

questions.title: Meaning of the slope
questions.prompt:
The cost \(C\), in euros, of renting a kayak for \(h\) hours is

\[C = 45 + 2.5h\]

What does 2.5 represent?
choices: The cost for each additional hour
The total cost for one hour
The number of hours that cost €45
questions.solution_title: The slope is the change per hour
questions.solution: Each extra hour adds €2.5 to \(C\). The fixed fee is 45; one hour costs \(45 + 2.5 = 47.5\).

questions.title: x-intercept from two points
questions.prompt:
A line passes through \((-3, 5)\) and \((6, -1)\).

What is the \(x\)-coordinate of its \(x\)-intercept?
questions.solution_title: Find the line, then set y = 0

questions.title: Parallel in standard form
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 2x + 5y = 10 &: \ m = -\tfrac{2}{5} \\ 4x + 10y = 3 &: \ m = -\tfrac{4}{10} \end{aligned}\]

\(-\tfrac{4}{10} = -\tfrac{2}{5}\): the same slope, a different line. \(-\tfrac{5}{2}\) is the perpendicular slope.

questions.title: Equation from a table
questions.prompt:
\[\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & 4 & 8 \\ \hline y & 9 & 15 & 21 \end{array}\]

Which equation fits the table?
questions.solution_title: Change in y over change in x
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} m &= \frac{15 - 9}{4 - 0} \\ &= \frac{3}{2} \end{aligned}\]

At \(x = 0\), \(y = 9\), so \(b = 9\). Choice \(6x\) uses the change in \(y\) only; \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) is the slope upside down.

takeaway: Slope is the change per unit and the intercept is the start; parallel lines share a slope and perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
